behaviors_covered: All eight complete research examples assert every output with explicit inputs and shared mod common.
RC low-pass: cutoff/scaling, negative phase, DC at minimum components and tiny positive attenuation.
RC high-pass: opposite corner phase, minimum positive frequency, high-frequency tiny phase/attenuation and DC rejection.
Second-order high-pass: Q-dependent true cutoff, pole gain KQ, half-power, inclusive Q endpoints and very small nonzero gain.
Deliyannis: resistor mapping/product, exact edge bandwidth/product, half-power edges, DC zero, exclusive Q=0.5, next representable Q and Q=50.
Butterworth: minimal feasible order, cutoff interval, nearest integer-boundary representation and both sides, adjacent positive losses, minimum edge ratio, 32 poles and all cross-input rejections.
Sallen–Key: capacitor labels, asymmetric resistor feedback weighting, DC, non-Butterworth half-power, Q endpoints and low-Q/high-Q/zero-damping/negative-damping rejection.
Fliege: DC unity, independent and reused center zero, near-notch positive gain, reciprocal-frequency symmetry, half-power edge identities and Q endpoints.
Buffered cascade: total cutoff, integer order endpoints, fractional rejection, DC, unwrapped phase, tiny attenuation and underflowed magnitude with finite dB.
Every scalar field: below/above bounds, zero-or-negative values, nonfinite inputs and subsequent valid recovery. Output-specific exact-zero or documented notch cancellation tolerances.
